items.weakness_text: Problem novelty/positioning: the failure modes (head-bias accumulation, tail erosion under EM) are not VLM-specific; they are general LT-TTA issues. The paper should sharpen what is uniquely VLM or reframe as a general LT-TTA method.

Model capacity: Results rely on low-capacity VLMs; validating on more powerful, recent VLMs would better establish its contribution and clarify whether gains persist or diminish with stronger backbones.

Limited methodological novelty: most core components (dual prototypes, rebalancing modules, entropy regularization) are adapted from existing long-tailed learning techniques, making the contribution incremental.
Computational overhead not fully analyzed: the proposed method introduces additional parameters; a detailed analysis of runtime and memory consumption is required.
Hyperparameter sensitivity: the method relies on several new hyperparameters (β in BEM, τ for temperature, η for CRA weighting) with limited analysis of sensitivity or tuning difficulty.
Intuition of synergy of SyPs and RS: the paper shows empirical synergy but lacks deeper explanation of why the two modules positively interact.
The method requires tuning several per-dataset hyperparameters, which contradicts the core objective of test-time adaptation, where models are expected to generalize without dataset-specific tuning.
Balanced Entropy Minimization (BEM) loss depends on access to class priors (π), which are not typically available in reality, making this assumption impractical.
Omission of discussion of important emerging TTA families (e.g., vision-encoder adaptation methods, parameter‑free approaches, reinforcement‑based TTA frameworks).
Notation and exposition can be difficult to follow; parts of the method are challenging to comprehend, affecting readability.
Long‑tailed TTA setting largely overlaps with non‑i.i.d. TTA studied in prior works; claim of being the first study is doubtful.
Proposed method appears similar to existing ones; BEM modification is close to class reweighting in non‑i.i.d. TTA, making the contribution incremental.
Section 2 lacks explicit discussion of non‑i.i.d. TTA; a subsection contrasting L‑TTA with prior studies is essential.
Table 4 omits training‑free TTA methods for VLMs (e.g., TDA, ZERO), which are critical for comparisons in speed/accuracy trade‑offs.
